question: Can a monotone bevel-law front concentrate slope toward the perimeter while an optically inferred positive back preserves the same physical source correspondence?
motivating_evidence: Root37 reviewed half-height, closed oval and full-height fronts. Full-height gives a broad pale band despite map preservation. Test curvature distribution, not more light or a new image operator.
initialization: The selected flat-front geometric map is a diagnostic design target, not photographic truth. No target image or source RGB is read.

fixed.front_depth: Half canonical spline central height, same as current working front center
fixed.front_power: Canonical full-spline global slope bound * radius / front_depth

unknown: One real radial back-height profile B, common to both lengths. Surface is reconstructed from optical boundary equations; no image displacement correction after tracing.
method: One inverse actual back ODE, same original physical map design prior. The front center height is anchored to current working; its edge slope matches the declared full-spline bound. No target pixel, free amplitude/exponent fit or source RGB.
checkpoint: Same-surface Snell equation sign, positive solve interval and finite budget before integration; positive/singlevalued endpoint and global profile bounds before any future forward render.
stop: One fixed anchored front construction. Stop first branch/positivity/invariant failure or original deadline. No second exponent/depth or profile smoothing. No native image before separate forward/source budget.
ownership: Root private experiment only, shared old tracer untouched during this design. Existing helper continues separate Search work through Sessionsation.
